beats.label: S1 · The stolen page
beats.text: Merchant survivor John Silver joins Flint's crew as cook, secretly holding the missing schedule page for the Spanish treasure galleon Urca de Lima.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up Silver's leverage over Flint and the season-long chase that drives every other plot.

beats.label: S1 · The frame-up
beats.text: Facing mutiny, Flint frames Singleton for the theft and executes him; only Gates and, soon, Billy Bones know the evidence was fabricated.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the secret that Billy will die for and that hangs over Flint's captaincy for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S1 · Eleanor picks Flint
beats.text: Eleanor breaks with Vane after his crew rapes Max, and partners with Flint to fund the Urca hunt through her father's smuggling network.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks in the Flint/Eleanor axis and the Eleanor/Vane rupture that structures Nassau politics from here on.

beats.label: S1 · The letter
beats.text: Flint captures the Andromache at heavy cost; Billy finds Mrs. Barlow's letter begging a pardon for Flint's murderous actions aboard the Maria Aleyne.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First crack in Flint's cover — Billy now suspects his captain has lied to the crew about who he is.

beats.label: S1 · Billy overboard
beats.text: Billy vanishes off the Walrus after confronting the letter; Flint tells the crew he fell, and no one else can prove otherwise.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the one man who could expose Flint and leaves an open thread the next season pays off.

beats.label: S1 · Vane retakes the fort
beats.text: Silver hands Flint the Urca schedule to save his own life; meanwhile Vane storms Hornigold's fort just as Nassau riots against Eleanor.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the guns of Nassau in Vane's hand and sets up the direct Flint/Vane collision of the next season.

beats.label: S1 · Flint kills Gates
beats.text: When Gates tries to abort the hunt, Flint smothers him; the Walrus then runs aground on the same shore as the beached Urca de Lima.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Flint has murdered his oldest friend and the gold is in sight — the exact position the season 2 premiere opens on.

cliffhanger.text: The Walrus is wrecked within sight of the Urca gold and a Spanish garrison. Flint has killed his closest friend to keep the hunt alive, and Nassau's fort now flies Vane's colours.
questions: Can Flint's beaten crew take the Spanish gold before the Royal Navy or the garrison acts?
Will Billy Bones surface again, and does he know what Flint actually did?
With Vane holding the fort and Eleanor's authority collapsing, who really runs Nassau?

characters.name: Captain Flint
characters.line: Brilliant, feared captain of the Walrus, obsessed with the Urca de Lima and hiding a past he will kill to protect.

characters.name: John Silver
characters.line: Opportunistic new cook who traded the schedule page for a berth in Flint's crew and is playing every side.

characters.name: Eleanor Guthrie
characters.line: Young woman running Nassau's smuggling fence, now bet on Flint after breaking with Vane.

characters.name: Charles Vane
characters.line: Rival pirate captain who has just retaken the fort and controls Nassau's cannon.

characters.name: Billy Bones
characters.line: Flint's loyal first mate, who found the letter, confronted Flint and vanished at sea.

characters.name: Jack Rackham
characters.line: Vane's former partner, now a struggling owner of the Nassau brothel with Max running the books.

characters.name: Anne Bonny
characters.line: Rackham's woman and knife hand, quietly involved with Max.

characters.name: Max
characters.line: Brothel prostitute, formerly Eleanor's lover, now aligned with Rackham after surviving Vane's crew.

characters.name: Miranda Barlow
characters.line: Flint's mysterious mainland companion, whose letter to a pardon-seeking clergyman began to expose him.

beats.label: S2 · Beached
beats.text: Walrus is stranded within sight of the Urca gold and a Spanish warship; Flint schemes his way back to captaincy by out-manoeuvring Dufresne.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets Flint's authority and puts the crew back in motion for everything that follows.

beats.label: S2 · Who Flint used to be
beats.text: Flashbacks reveal Flint was a Royal Navy lieutenant, in love with Thomas Hamilton, whose plan to pardon Nassau's pirates cost Flint his rank and his life.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The engine of every choice Flint makes from here — his war is Thomas's dream, and Miranda holds the receipts.

beats.label: S2 · Abigail Ashe
beats.text: Vane storms Ned Low's ship and takes Abigail Ashe, daughter of Carolina's governor, intending to ransom her back to the mainland.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The hostage that Flint and Miranda will pivot the whole pardon plan around.

beats.label: S2 · Miranda's pivot
beats.text: Miranda Barlow — formerly Mrs. Hamilton — reaches Flint mid-bombardment and turns him from war on Vane to trading Abigail for Peter Ashe's protection.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Redirects the season from military to diplomatic and puts Miranda back at the centre of Flint's world.

beats.label: S2 · Silver's cut, Silver's leg
beats.text: Silver secretly feeds the Urca's location to Rackham to grab the gold behind Flint's back; captured and tortured, he loses his leg but keeps the secret.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Marks Silver's turn into an operator with his own agenda, and physically changes him for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S2 · Charles Town betrays them
beats.text: Peter Ashe hands Flint over for public execution; Miranda is shot dead in the negotiation and the pardon plan dies with her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills the woman anchoring Flint to peace and gives him the personal reason to burn the empire down.

beats.label: S2 · Vane saves Flint
beats.text: Vane's crew shells Charles Town, breaks Flint out and murders Ashe; the two former enemies sail home while Rackham quietly lands the Urca gold in Nassau.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Forges the Flint/Vane alliance and hands Rackham the reputation that will define the next season's power struggle.

cliffhanger.text: Flint returns to Nassau bound to Vane and hollowed out by Miranda's death. Rackham, once a joke, walks in with the Spanish fortune while Silver hides both his leg and his stake.
questions: What does Flint want now that Peter Ashe is dead and Miranda's pardon plan has died with her?
How long can Silver hide his cut of the gold and his role in stealing it from Flint?
Now that London knows pirates have the Urca, what response is coming for Nassau?

characters.name: Captain Flint
characters.line: Broken by Miranda's murder, allied with his old enemy Vane, and no longer chasing a pardon but a reckoning.

characters.name: John Silver
characters.line: One-legged crewman who quietly stole the gold from Flint and is trusted by no one who knows what he did.

characters.name: Charles Vane
characters.line: The man who rescued Flint from the gallows and now his uneasy ally in whatever comes next.

characters.name: Jack Rackham
characters.line: Nassau's new pirate hero after landing the Urca fortune, no longer written off as a joke.

characters.name: Anne Bonny
characters.line: At Rackham's side and increasingly wary of Max's growing influence over him.

characters.name: Max
characters.line: Brothel madam turned political fixer, quietly building a power base underneath everyone.

characters.name: Eleanor Guthrie
characters.line: Seized by mutinous crewmen and handed to the Royal Navy for pardons; last seen bound for London.
characters.note: Not in Nassau at the end of the season.

characters.name: Billy Bones
characters.line: Alive and back with the crew, saying nothing about the letter or Flint's real past.

beats.label: S3 · Flint's total war
beats.text: Flint wages open war on any ship supporting pardons; Silver, now hardened, thinks the campaign is turning reckless and suicidal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the Flint/Silver split that drives every later argument about how far to take the fight.

beats.label: S3 · Rogers arrives
beats.text: Woodes Rogers lands with royal pardons and the fleet to enforce them; Rackham blows the fort so Vane can escape aboard the returning Blackbeard's ship.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The new governor is the season's antagonist and the reason every pirate must choose a side.

beats.label: S3 · The Maroon island
beats.text: The Walrus is wrecked on a hidden island of escaped slaves; their Queen is revealed to be Mr. Scott's wife, and the crew's lives hang on her ruling.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Maroons as the pirates' only real ally against Britain and sets up their war economy.

beats.label: S3 · Silver and Madi
beats.text: Silver bonds with the Queen's daughter Madi and helps broker a formal alliance between the Walrus crew and the Maroons.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The relationship that will eventually decide Silver's loyalties and the shape of the whole war.

beats.label: S3 · Vane is hanged
beats.text: Rogers captures Vane; Eleanor, now his lover and partner, insists on hanging Charles publicly in the Nassau square.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes one of the show's core pirates and gives Blackbeard and Rackham the personal cause to attack Nassau.

beats.label: S3 · Blackbeard turns the tide
beats.text: Blackbeard's fleet arrives to avenge Vane; with Rackham and Anne aboard, they drive the Royal Navy off the beach in a bloody rout.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The military reset that leaves Nassau contested rather than lost, and puts pirates back on the offensive.

beats.label: S3 · The Long John Silver myth
beats.text: Billy murders a pardoned captain in Nassau, leaves the Black Spot and claims the killing in the name of Long John Silver.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Manufactures the legend around Silver that will become the pirates' rallying banner going forward.

cliffhanger.text: The pirates and Maroons have driven the Royal Navy off the beach, but Rogers still governs and Nassau is still contested. Vane is dead, Blackbeard has come back to war, and the name Long John Silver is spreading through the town without Silver's consent.
questions: What does a wounded, defeated Rogers reach for next to hold Nassau?
Can Silver live up to the legend Billy is building around him, and does he want to?
How long will the Maroons stay in this war once they see how much blood the pirates will spend?

characters.name: Captain Flint
characters.line: Committed to burning the empire down, allied with the Maroons and Blackbeard against Rogers.

characters.name: John Silver
characters.line: Crippled crewman turned uneasy folk-hero, in love with Madi and increasingly the pirates' public face.

characters.name: Madi
characters.line: Daughter of the Maroon Queen and Mr. Scott, Silver's partner and the moral centre of the alliance.

characters.name: Woodes Rogers
characters.line: British governor of Nassau, weakened by fever after the battle but still in office and still Eleanor's husband in ambition.

characters.name: Eleanor Guthrie
characters.line: Rogers' lover and partner, personally responsible for Vane's hanging and reviled by the pirates for it.

characters.name: Edward Teach (Blackbeard)
characters.line: Returned pirate legend, now bound to Rackham and Anne by Vane's death and leading the fleet at sea.

characters.name: Jack Rackham
characters.line: Sailing with Blackbeard, out for revenge on Rogers and Nassau's British rulers.

characters.name: Billy Bones
characters.line: On the island building the Long John Silver myth, killing pardoned captains to sell the story.

characters.name: Max
characters.line: Nassau's political operator, tied to Rogers and Eleanor's project of turning the town legitimate.

beats.label: S4 · The trap on the beach
beats.text: Flint and Blackbeard's assault on Nassau collapses into an ambush; 121 pirates and Maroons are captured and marched off for execution.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The military failure that forces every faction to change strategy for the rest of the season.

beats.label: S4 · Billy breaks with Flint
beats.text: Billy decides Nassau belongs to pirates alone and turns on Flint and the Maroons; he begins quietly feeding intelligence to Rogers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splits the pirate side in two and gives Rogers his most valuable informant inside the town.

beats.label: S4 · Spain burns Nassau
beats.text: Flint retakes Nassau; Rogers sails to Havana and returns with a Spanish fleet that levels the town and scatters everyone into the interior.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The physical destruction that ends any illusion Nassau can be held as a pirate republic.

beats.label: S4 · Rogers's lie about Madi
beats.text: Rogers captures Madi and tells Silver she is dead; the news breaks Silver and privately turns him against Flint's war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rewires Silver's motives and sets up the private betrayal that ends the pirate cause.

beats.label: S4 · Jack goes to Philadelphia
beats.text: Jack and Max sail to Philadelphia to make a deal with Eleanor's grandmother Marion Guthrie for Nassau's post-war economy.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Opens the diplomatic track that will actually decide Nassau's future while Flint fights the losing war.

beats.label: S4 · Skeleton Island
beats.text: Flint buries the war chest on Skeleton Island; Rogers ambushes the fleet and Silver's ship burns as his men die around him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The disaster that leaves Silver with nothing but the treasure and his private plan for it.

beats.label: S4 · Flint sails for Savannah
beats.text: Jack helps break Rogers with Marion's money; Silver learns Madi lives, and Flint chooses to leave for Savannah rather than continue the war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the war, ends Flint's arc as a pirate, and hands Nassau's future to Rackham and Max.

cliffhanger.text: Nassau is quiet on the surface: Rogers is finished in debt, Jack and Max hold the town through the Guthries, and Flint has left for Savannah. Silver has Madi back but has spent every alliance he had to buy her.
questions: Can what Silver has built with Madi survive her knowing what he did to end the war?
How long does Rackham and Max's arrangement with Marion Guthrie actually hold Nassau together?
With Flint gone and the treasure buried, what is left of the pirate cause that Billy fought for?

characters.name: John Silver
characters.line: Ended the war behind Flint's back to save Madi; keeps the buried treasure and no clean conscience.

characters.name: Captain Flint
characters.line: Sent to Savannah rather than allowed to keep fighting, his war on the empire finished by Silver's choice.

characters.name: Madi
characters.line: Alive and freed, back with Silver but knowing he has traded the Maroon cause for her.

characters.name: Jack Rackham
characters.line: Architect of Nassau's new economic order through Marion Guthrie, and Vane's avenger against Rogers.

characters.name: Anne Bonny
characters.line: At Rackham's side through Philadelphia and the final battle, one of the few relationships still intact.

characters.name: Max
characters.line: Nassau's political broker between the Guthries, the pirates and the returning legitimate order.

characters.name: Woodes Rogers
characters.line: Defeated, bankrupt and bought out by Marion Guthrie; no longer a threat to anyone.

characters.name: Billy Bones
characters.line: Broken with Flint and drawn into Rogers's orbit, his Long John Silver myth turned against its subject.

characters.name: Marion Guthrie
characters.line: Eleanor's grandmother in Philadelphia, the money and the political weight now underwriting Nassau.
